handoffs.message: Chair reassigned owner from Codex2 to Codex: PINT-002 is a non-human blocked task with Codex supplied as a healthy rescue target; redispatch must still wait for the missing PINT-001 additive contract freeze. Task returned to todo for a blocked-owner rescue dispatch.

Implemented idempotent contextual workshop resolution, fail-closed included/excluded Persona eligibility, and typed analysis-only interaction submission. Anchor d20a38f72. Verified: 207 Agora tests passed.

Reopened: tenant isolation fail-open in participant eligibility. In services/control-plane/bff/agora/interaction/router.py eligibility(), the tenant check at line ~113 is 'str(persona.get("tenant_id") or resolved.tenant_id) != resolved.tenant_id', which always evaluates false when persona.tenant_id is missing/None -- so any persona lacking an explicit tenant_id is silently treated as belonging to every tenant and included with zero reasons. Verified with a live repro: a persona record with tenant_id=None from another tenant context is returned in 'included' with no tenant_mismatch reason, while a persona with an explicit different tenant_id is correctly excluded. This contradicts the task's 'fail-closed' acceptance criterion and is inconsistent with session_for()'s correct fail-closed pattern (session.get('tenant_id') != resolved.tenant_id, no fallback) in the same file. Required fix: drop the 'or resolved.tenant_id' fallback so a missing/None tenant_id fails closed (adds tenant_mismatch), matching session_for's pattern. Also worth a look: context:resolve's Idempotency-Key replay does not fingerprint the request body, so a reused key with a different payload silently returns the first cached response -- confirm this is intentional before closing. Tests still pass (22 passed) because the existing suite never exercises a persona record with a missing/None tenant_id.

Tenant isolation now fails closed for personas with missing/None tenant_id; regression coverage added. Context replay remains the original same-key replay contract (no payload-conflict expansion). Verified: 22 focused tests passed. Commits: d20a38f72, 0481cf650.

Independently re-verified: router wiring into create_agora_router matches sibling routers, workshop_store field usage matches strategy_workshop/store.py, fail-closed tenant_mismatch fix in 0481cf650 is correct (removed the resolved.tenant_id fallback that let unscoped personas pass). Ran pytest services/control-plane/bff/tests/test_agora_persona_interactions.py services/control-plane/bff/tests/test_agora_router.py -q: 22 passed. Acceptance criteria met (idempotent context resolution, eligibility reasons, fail-closed permissions).

blockers.message: Blocked by incomplete PINT-001 contract freeze: merged Agora v1.6 bundle defines only persona opinion consultation and governed action authority events with implementation_status=contract_frozen_no_backend_routes. It does not define contextual workshop resolution, participant eligibility/recommendation, or typed interaction submission schemas/routes/capabilities/ETag/idempotency rules. docs/product/persona-interaction-and-governed-action-plan.md section 10 explicitly says implementation tasks must not guess these decisions. PINT-001 owner must add and merge the missing additive contracts/examples before PINT-002 can implement safely.

PINT-001 merged event-only schemas but did not freeze the exact BFF routes, request/response schemas, contextual reference verification contract, eligibility reason model, environment/capability gates, or idempotency semantics required by PINT-002. capability_manifest_v1_6.json explicitly says no backend routes, while the accepted product plan forbids implementation tasks from guessing them. Waiting for PINT-001 contract owner to publish an additive BFF/OpenAPI freeze before implementation.
